title: A new species of Pimelodella (Heptapteridae: Rhamdiinae) from the upper Bermejo basin, northwestern La Plata basin
content:
Abstract

A new species of Pimelodella occurring in the upper Bermejo basin is described using morphological and genetic data. The new species is distinguished from most congeners by having fewer total vertebrae (37–39), short adipose-fin base (20.3%–25.2% of L S), maxillary barbel almost reaching or reaching the origin of the adipose fin, subequal lobes of caudal fin or upper lobe slightly longer, supraoccipital process articulating with the anterior nuchal plate and epiphyseal branch of supraorbital canal on the head ending in a single sensory pore (s6 + s6). The type locality of the new species is situated in the transition zone between the Yunga and Dry Chaco terrestrial ecoregions near the area of influence of Parque Nacional El Rey. Considering the high anthropogenic impact resulting from agricultural activities in the region and the high level of endemism present in the upper Bermejo basin, the new species could be categorized as Endangered (EN) in a future formal assessment, following the IUCN criteria.
